item.title: Israel Olaleye: How Can Young Nigerians Buy Land & Properties Legitimately Today?
item.description: Young man with a hard hat holding a red for sale sign outside a building by Pavel Danilyuk for Pexels . My parents’ generation mostly bought land the way their parents did. Someone in the family knew someone in the village. An uncle walked the boundaries. The community remembered who owned what, and if anything went wrong, you had a face to go back to. However, my generation buys land on Instagram. I do not say that to mock anyone. I sell land for a living. When I started in real estate sales in 2023, two years after finishing a Mathematics degree at the University of Ibadan, I assumed buyers would care most about price and location. They do care. But what I hear most often is fear, dressed up as questions. Can I trust you? Is this land real? What happens if I miss a payment? After I pay, will someone come and ask me for more money? A prospective buyer once asked me, before anything else, whether community or family payments would follow after she paid for her plot. She was not asking about the land. She was asking whether the price I quoted was the real price. She had good reason to ask. Lagos State’s Property Protection Law of 2016 made it an offence to demand levies for construction on someone else’s property. Yet the same law still allows a land-owning family, with the family head’s authority, to collect a customary fee for possession, the payment many people know as a “foundation levy”. So the honest answer to her question is not a simple yes or no. It depends on the land, the family, and what has been written down. Most first-time buyers have never been told any of this. That is the gap I keep coming back to. Nobody taught us how to buy land. We learned how to save. Some of us learned how to invest in stocks, crypto or a side business. But land, the asset our parents spoke about with the most respect, has no manual. The people who used to stand in for the manual–the uncle, the community, the family lawyer everyone trusted–are often not part of how we buy anymore. So we improvise. A prospect once told me she had gone through my Instagram page carefully before she agreed to speak with me. She was checking whether I was consistent, whether my posts matched what I said on the phone, whether I had been around long enough to be real. I was flattered. Then I was worried. Because if a social media page has become part of a buyer’s due diligence, then a polished page has also become one of the easiest ways to deceive her. Instagram cannot tell you who owns a piece of land. Only a search at the land registry, done by your own lawyer, can begin to tell you that. Instagram cannot tell you whether a plot sits under government acquisition or on a planned road. A surveyor who charts the coordinates and checks them against official maps can. No number of testimonials replaces a written contract that states what you are paying for, what you are not paying for, and what happens if a payment is missed. None of this is complicated. item.title: Astronomers watch a red giant star greedily devour a stellar 'Bao bun' before erupting: 'We couldn't quite believe our luck'
item.description: null Astronomers witnessed the spectacular cosmic indigestion that resulted from a red giant star that devoured a stellar Bao bun in the form of its smaller companion star. That isn't a random comparison. The cannibal star, which is 350 times bigger than the sun, is nicknamed "Big Bao," while its unfortunate companion had the nickname "Little Bao." The cute cosmic monikers come from the fact that this destructive merger event has been designated AT2025abao. A Bao bun might be a little snack for a human, but this red giant star made a real meal out of Little Bao. This cannibalistic event was tracked by a wide array of ground- and space-based telescopes, including NASA space missions NEOWISE, SPHEREx, and the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), as well as the W. M. Keck Observatory in Hawaii. The conclusion of the event AT2025abao was marked by a massive eruption witnessed in Oct. 2025 by two instruments at Caltech's Palomar Observatory: the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) and the Wide-field INfrared Transient ExploreR (WINTER). "The excitement was real," team member Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University said in a statement sent to Space.com via email. "We couldn't quite believe our luck. With detailed observations for several years before the merger, for the first time, we now have an unprecedented glimpse of the conditions that lead to such cosmic events." Reconstructing a violent cosmic collision The story of AT2025abao began when astronomers detected a bright flash in the nearby Andromeda galaxy , a region where scientists hadn't expected to see a cosmic explosion. Responding to this unexpected flash, Karambelkar and colleagues set about investigating its cause with a plethora of telescopes. This led to them seeing a slow and continuous brightening over the course of two years, They determined the cause of the flash was a rare stellar merger, the luminous red nova now designated AT2025abao. They linked this to a star called WNTR23bzdiq / WTP19aalzlk that had been observed steadily brightening since 2019 after being stable for the preceding 30 years. Thus, the team determined that at the heart of the event is a red giant, a star that puffs out to hundreds of times its original size after it runs out of hydrogen in its core. The team theorizes that Big Bao, with a mass seven times greater than the sun, expanded so rapidly and violently that it swallowed its smaller companion star. The unfortunate star, Little Bao, then spiraled into Big Bao's core in fewer than 10 orbits. "A couple of years back, we discovered a star that was gradually brightening. We took a closer look to discover a red giant, or a star that has started to expand toward the end of its life, just like our sun will one day," Karambelkar said. "Steady brightening was unusual, but even if something was stirring, no one expected to see an explosion in their lifetime, as these stars remain relatively stable for thousands of years." item.title: Nathan Lyon faces Australia axe with bowler accused in fresh ball tampering allegations
item.description: Nathan Lyon is set to be dropped by Australia for their next Test match and the spin bowler has been accused in fresh ball tampering accusations in the aftermath of Sandpapergate . Reports emerged that the 39-year-old spinner is set to be dropped when the squad for next month’s first Test against New Zealand is announced on Saturday. Having previously been squeezed out of the first XI on several occasions recently, he is now tipped to lose his squad place to Corey Rocchiccioli. Lyon is the sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 wickets and had worked hard to recover from a hamstring injury last summer in order to return to the Test side. The news comes as Code Sports alleged Lyon was the previously unnamed player who suggested using mints to shine the ball against Pakistan in the first match after South Africa only to be angrily shot down by new head coach Justin Langer. Lyon has yet to respond publicly. Meanwhile, Australia’s conduct during the 2017/18 Ashes is back under the microscope after the independent forum set up to explore the ‘sandpapergate’ scandal was handed an expanded brief. Earlier this month, Cricket Australia reacted to a barrage of claims and counter-claims from former players by announcing that all players and staff members would be invited to share their recollections of the ill-fated 2018 South Africa tour in a ‘safe space’. Lyon is the sixth leading wicket-taker of all time with 577 wickets and had worked hard to recover from a hamstring injury last summer in order to return to the Test side (PA Archive) CA has now formalised the terms of reference and opted to add the previous home summer – when Australia beat England 4-0 to reclaim the urn – to its scope. A statement confirmed the forum would hear accounts related to “ball-management practices in the Australian Men’s Team during the 2017/18 season, all four Tests of the 2018 SA Tour, the events of 24 March 2018, (and) the conduct and scope of the 2018 CA investigation”. Usman Khawaja, whose autobiography reopened the historic drama, has alleged that ball-tampering methods were being utilised prior to South Africa and Cameron Bancroft – who was caught red-handed in Cape Town with sandpaper – has written about being urged to manipulate the quarter-seam on his Test debut against England in Brisbane. Those claims have brought to light a passage in Sir Alastair Cook’s own memoir, published in 2019, in which he alleges David Warner admitted during a post-series drink to using substances in his finger strapping to deteriorate the ball. Warner has admitted his involvement in the sandpaper episode but responded to subsequent reporting about his using superglue and grit, by stating: “I would suggest establishing the facts rather than perpetuating speculation”. England have maintained near total silence on the subject during their recent white-ball tour of Australia. item.title: Ruben Amorim apologises for Diego Moreira's provocative celebration after AC Milan's stunning Olympiacos comeback
item.description: FBL-EUR-C3-OLYMPIACOS-MILAN - AFP AC Milan manager Ruben Amorim was forced to issue a formal apology following a heated conclusion to his side's Europa League victory in Greece. The Portuguese coach addressed the friction caused by winger Diego Moreira, whose defiant actions overshadowed a brilliant rossoneri comeback. Amorim addresses Moreira’s controversial conduct Amorim found himself playing the role of peacemaker following Milan’s 4-2 victory over Olympiacos on Thursday night. The match ended in a state of high tension after Moreira, who scored the final goal to secure the win, celebrated in a way that deeply offended the home supporters and the Greek side's technical staff. The winger stood motionless, staring down the stands for several seconds in a gesture viewed as an intentional provocation. The young winger's actions immediately sparked a confrontation on the pitch, with Olympiacos players Jota Silva and Saliakas rushing to challenge the Milan man. The atmosphere at the Karaiskakis Stadium turned toxic in the final moments as the home side took exception to the disrespect shown following the fourth goal. "It won't happen again. Moreira is a young man who plays, but he needs to grow. We know we wouldn't like it if they did it to our fans. It's my responsibility, but he didn't do it in a mean way. I apologize, but he didn't do it in a mean way," Amorim said, as quoted by TuttoMercatoWeb . Hutchinson proves to be the difference-maker Beyond the controversy, Omari Hutchinson emerged as the game’s standout performer, justifying the club’s faith in him during the summer transfer window. Amorim dismissed the idea that he alone was responsible for the signing, insisting that the recruitment process at Milan is a collective effort. The former Ipswich Town man changed the dynamic of the game as a second-half substitute, driving his side toward the 4-2 result. "When we do something in the club we are all on board. If someone doesn't agree on a player, we turn elsewhere. When someone arrives it's because everyone believes in the player. We needed a player with those characteristics. Sometimes you see the talent. He had a difficult season at Nottingham but did well at Ipswich. He is very strong at playing in tight spaces. He has the potential to do more, especially with the shirt. He can make those runs with the ball more often," the coach revealed. Tactical shifts and injury concerns The match turned on several key tactical decisions , though Amorim was modest about his role in the comeback. The withdrawal of Goncalo Ramos raised eyebrows among the travelling fans, but the coach clarified that the substitution was forced rather than tactical. This paved the way for a more aggressive approach that eventually overwhelmed the Greek side's defence during a frantic second half. "I didn't change the game. Ramos came off because he was in pain. item.title: 'I don't like it!' - Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho shuts down Zinedine Zidane comparisons after Jude Bellingham's Champions League masterclass
item.description: Real Madrid C.F. v PSV Eindhoven - UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 - Getty Images Sport Jose Mourinho has shut down comparisons between Jude Bellingham and Zinedine Zidane following Real Madrid's emphatic 5-1 Champions League victory over PSV Eindhoven. The Portuguese manager addressed the growing hype during Friday's press conference, offering a measured verdict on how the two midfield greats should be viewed. Mourinho shuts down Zidane comparisons Mourinho has distanced himself from the growing debate linking Bellingham to Zidane. The comparisons surfaced earlier this week after the England midfielder delivered a standout display in Europe. Bellingham drew widespread acclaim following Tuesday's 5-1 Champions League triumph over PSV. His commanding performance prompted observers to draw parallels with the legendary French playmaker. However, when asked about the link during his media duties on Friday, Mourinho made it clear he has no interest in pitting the two players against each other. Different eras, same elite status Rather than weighing one midfielder's qualities against the other, the Portuguese tactician stressed that both players deserve to be judged strictly within their own eras. Mourinho believes generational gaps make direct comparisons pointless. "I don't like comparing footballers from different generations," Mourinho told reporters on Friday. "Zidane was one of the best of his generation and Jude is already one of the best of his." Bellingham's impressive numbers and humble view The praise surrounding Bellingham has been fuelled by his consistent output throughout the current campaign. At just 23 years old, the midfielder has already registered seven goals in 18 appearances across all competitions for Madrid this season. His display in the five-goal rout of PSV only intensified the spotlight. Yet despite his rapid rise and growing influence in Madrid, the England international remains grounded about his place in football history. When previously confronted with the same comparisons, Bellingham himself played down the hype , insisting that Zidane was "much better" than him. Focus on Alaves Bellingham and his teammates are currently preparing to face Deportivo Alaves at the Santiago Bernabeu in their upcoming Liga fixture. The England international will look to contribute once again for Los Blancos as they aim to secure all three points in front of their home supporters. Madrid currently sit second in the league standings with 33 points from 13 matches - three points behind the league leaders, Barcelona.

item.title: ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany
item.description: ANALYSIS | This is why Werder Bremen is No.1 in northern Germany Werder Bremen is the best team in northern Germany. At least that is what was evident from last weekend’s Nordderby, when they successfully beat Hamburg 4–0 at the Weserstadion. Bremen did more than just win that game; they demonstrated their quality this season and their ability to maximise the potential of their players to become a highly efficient team. This is the issue: The underlying numbers, in this case expected goals (xG), indicate that the game was actually very close – not as one-sided as the result suggests. HSV even had 1.54 compared to Bremen’s 1.52 in front of xG, per Opta. So, being able to win by a four-goal margin despite losing on xG shows just how effective Bremen are as a team. Get German Football News’ Bergas investigates why… First thing first: Underlying numbers need context Yes, HSV has more numbers in front of xG. However, if we look at the xG data itself, 1.03 of HSV’s 1.54 came after they fell behind in the 55th minute. In this situation, the state of the game changed, with HSV adopting a more proactive approach with the ball. Meanwhile, between minutes 1 and 54, when the score was still 0–0, HSV only achieved an xG of 0.5 (Bremen had 0.84). This is why xG is not the best metric with which to measure HSV’s performance in this game, because the state of the game forced them to create more chances in order to catch up, resulting in lots of shots. In fact, however, they weren’t really dangerous enough to challenge or harm Bremen. Looking at other metrics such as key passes, HSV weren’t superior either during the even time when the score was still 0–0. In that period, they made four key passes compared to Bremen’s eight. HSV found it much harder to create shots than the home team. Even in the first half, when Bremen were underperforming in parts, HSV didn’t look particularly threatening. Bremen flexible defensive structure made HSV toothless One of the reasons for that is Bremen’s flexibility in their approach to HSV when defending. In the first half, they often used a man-to-man approach (which was more aggressive), which successfully forced HSV to use long balls to progress the ball to the final third, particularly on their left side. In this long-ball scenario, Bremen also had the advantage when it came to closing down HSV attacks. The problem for Bremen arose when HSV successfully won the second ball, creating a situation in which Amos Pieper had to defend one-on-one against the opponent. Pieper struggled in the early stages of the game against HSV’s pacey attackers and received a yellow card in the first half, but played safely for the rest of the game and successfully avoided another red card. This was also thanks to Bremen’s improved defensive structure in the second half. They were not as aggressive as before, but rather kept their double six close to their defensive line. With this defensive structure, HSV were unable to find the free space in front

item.title: Michigan State football vs. Rutgers: 5 determining factors and a prediction
item.description: Lansing State Journal columnist Graham Couch looks at Michigan State's game at Rutgers. When: 4:15 p.m. Saturday. Where: SHI Stadium, Piscataway, New Jersey California. TV: Big Ten Network. Betting line: MSU -3.5. 1. Kayd Coffman, Start No. 3 MSU freshman quarterback Kayd Coffman’s progress from his first start against UCLA to his second against Oregon was tangible — highlighted by an 8-for-9 passing stretch in the first half and a third-quarter touchdown drive when he really settled in. MSU offensive coordinator Nick Sheridan said Coffman’s progress was also evident based on his demeanor, confidence, poise and interactions during the game. Start No. 3 for Coffman comes with realistic hopes of a win for the first time. And the need for a sound performance from him. If he struggles, senior Cam Fancher is listed as questionable on MSU's injury report and could be available. But this appears to be Coffman's show Saturday. Coffman threw an interception to a linebacker in each of his first two starts. Avoiding that would go a ways toward helping the Spartans ' cause. He also didn't finish either game, because they were lopsided and so Leo Hannan came in to finish them. This is likely to be Coffman’s first collegiate game playing in crunch time, in a game likely to be decided in the fourth quarter, in part on his arm and decisions. We’ll see how he handles it. 2. Containing Antwan Raymond and Rutgers’ running game Rutgers has one of the better running backs in the Big Ten in Antwan Raymond, who’s put together some notable performances — rushing 18 times for 150 yards against Northwestern, averaging 7.7 yards per carry against Michigan and, last week, carrying 23 times for 101 in the upset of Penn State (not counting his lateral to a teammate for the last-second touchdown, a play he was banged up on; he's listed as questionable against MSU). Raymond is a quick and shifty back. His backup, Clay Thevenin, is also averaging 5.0 yards per carry. This is a Rutgers running game that, when the offensive line does its part, is pretty effective. The Scarlet Knights are a lot less threatening through the air, but if they start to get downhill on you, it’s a respectable offense — one that scored 21 points against Michigan and 25 against Penn State. 3. For MSU, one last day in the fight There have been signs in the second halves of MSU’s last two games that the Spartans are wearing down — and obviously wearing thin at certain positions. MSU has done an incredible job of showing up each week, outside of perhaps the Wisconsin game. It’s been a testament to the character of the players and the culture developing in the program. At some point, though, you’d think the Spartans might be due for a day when they aren’t quite as up for it. Given that so many MSU players are playing their final college games, including several who’ve battled back from injury to play again — like running back Jaziun Patterson and cornerback Tre Bell — it’s hard to imagine this is a let-up spo

item.title: ‘Heal faster than Wolverine’ – LA Lakers fans can’t believe Dylan Harper’s crazy injury recovery
item.description: Photo by Katelyn Mulcahy/Getty Images Dylan Harper’s latest injury update has Los Angeles Lakers fans in disbelief. San Antonio Spurs star Dylan Harper has been sidelined with a hip injury, which he picked up during the team’s 103-95 loss against the Detroit Pistons earlier in the month. Harper was expected to be sidelined for at least one to three weeks, with two weeks a likely return, but the team’s latest injury report has upgraded him to questionable ahead of facing the Los Angeles Lakers. The update has the Lakers fanbase in disbelief, as they recalled a popular joke about opposing teams’ injured players magically healing before facing the 17-time NBA champions. LA Lakers fans react to Dylan Harper potentially returning If Harper follows the initial recovery schedule, he would miss facing the Spurs vs. Lakers’ NBA Cup Group Stage clash. However, as mentioned earlier, the Spurs have upgraded their star guard to questionable before taking on the Purple and Gold. If Harper plays, it would mean he missed just 10 days after suffering a hip injury, and this has Lakers fans in disbelief. “Players heal faster than Wolverine when they see Lakers on the schedule,” a frustrated fan wrote. While another simply added, “Would not be surprised if Fox would magically play too.” “Magical healing powers when Luka is next on the schedule,” a third fan pointed out. However, a fourth fan called out the X post, stating: “Right in that range of the 1-3 week timetable. Thanks.” A fifth fan added, “Everybody wants to play the Lakers for their Super Bowl.” A sixth announced, “Death taxes and players magically healing up when the Lakers are on their schedule.” Even head coach JJ Redick once expressed his surprise over how players magically heal when they have the Lakers on their schedule. But as far as Harper’s return is concerned, it’s not that surprising. After all, the return falls in the one-to-three-week range. item.title: Powerful Storm Disrupts US Thanksgiving, Leaves Over 900,000 Without Power
item.description: A powerful storm disrupted Thanksgiving celebrations for millions of Americans on Thursday, as New York’s famed Macy’s parade was postponed for the first time in its 100-year history. Heavy rain and strong winds from the “Nor-easter” battered the central and eastern United States, creating treacherous travel conditions during one of the country’s busiest holiday periods. As families were gathering for traditional holiday feasts, more than 900,000 homes and businesses were without power, with Pennsylvania, Maryland and Virginia particularly hard hit, according to tracking website PowerOutage. At airports, nearly 400 flights were cancelled, and over 2,000 were delayed in the United States, mostly in the East, figures from FlightAware showed. New York’s famed parade, which sees brightly colored balloons travel through the heart of Manhattan, was pushed back to Saturday due to what organisers said was an “abundance of caution.” Millions of people typically gather to catch a glimpse of the festivities. The only other time the parade was not held on Thanksgiving Thursday was when it was cancelled for three years during World War II. Organisers would have been only too aware of the gusting winds that wrecked the parade back in 1997 when a careening 18-foot figure of the “Cat in the Hat” toppled a lamppost, knocking one bystander unconscious. “While we are heartbroken that our parade was postponed, the safety of our partners, the safety of our participants — and spectators — is and always will be our top priority,” said Macy’s parade executive producer Will Coss. Stay Safe People brave the bad weather in the Manhattan borough of New York City on November 26, 2026. Photo by KENA BETANCUR / AFP While flooding was reported up and down the East Coast, impacts were also felt inland, with powerful gusts and inundated soil leading to trees tumbling over onto power lines and homes. Authorities in the Maryland suburbs of the US capital, worried about the impact of power outages on the water treatment network, asked nearly two million customers to conserve tap water consumption. Officials urged people to limit road travel, while several major bridges were closed due to high winds. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, who declared a state of emergency Wednesday over the weather, urged residents to take precautions to stay safe. “Keep your devices charged, report power outages directly to your utility provider, and stay away from downed power lines,” she wrote on X. Some people improvised to still enjoy Thanksgiving, which is traditionally marked by gathering with family around a large meal, with turkey as the centerpiece. “No electricity? No problem,” celebrity chef Jose Andres wrote on X, alongside a video of a candlelit dining room and lobsters cooking on a gas-powered stove. The East Coast disruption came as Californians also suffered weather woes this week, with massive waves battering the coast, prompting evacuations in some areas and soaking San Francisco. The

item.title: Liverpool make transfer decision ahead of January window
item.description: Liverpool make transfer decision ahead of January window Jeremie Frimpong Faces Big Liverpool Test Under Andoni Iraola Jeremie Frimpong’s first start in Liverpool’s 3-0 Champions League win over Club Brugge felt significant for more than the result. After an injury-hit spell and a stop-start first year at Anfield, the 25-year-old is trying to re-establish himself in a position that remains open, competitive and still under assessment. According to the Daily Mail, Frimpong has no desire to move on despite reported Saudi Arabia interest. His focus is on staying at Liverpool and proving himself to Andoni Iraola. That determination will matter, because the head coach has already shown he values intensity, direct running and aggressive full-back play, traits Frimpong naturally brings. Liverpool invested £29.5 million to sign him from Bayer Leverkusen, backing a player with a strong reputation in the Bundesliga and across Europe. Yet his first season on Merseyside never found full rhythm. Injury disruption and inconsistency limited his wider impact, with 35 appearances, two goals and two assists across all competitions. Photo: IMAGO Right-back battle remains open The broader picture adds intrigue. Conor Bradley has also endured fitness frustrations, while Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona and primarily a centre-back, has stepped in at right-back to strong effect. His displays have given Iraola a dependable option, one that appears to offer balance and reliability in and out of possession. That leaves Frimpong with a clear challenge. His attacking strengths are obvious, pace, width, energy and a willingness to drive Liverpool forward. He can stretch teams and create overloads, particularly when matches become open. Those qualities suit Iraola’s football. Defensive questions still need answering The concern is whether Frimpong can offer enough defensive control in a back four over a sustained period. Liverpool need a right-back who can recover quickly, protect space behind him and stay disciplined when the game turns. That part of the role will shape how Iraola judges him over the months ahead. Frimpong’s return has arrived at an important moment. He has the talent to become a valuable Liverpool option, and perhaps more than that, but the next phase is about trust. If he can show growth without the ball, this conversation shifts quickly. If he cannot, Liverpool may yet revisit the market. Our View This feels like one of the more fascinating subplots in Liverpool’s squad planning. Frimpong is the kind of player supporters enjoy watching because everything he does seems to have urgency. He carries threat, he pushes the line back and he gives the side a different attacking rhythm almost immediately. At the same time, there is a reason this debate keeps resurfacing. Right-back under Iraola has to be about judgement as much as adventure. Timing matters. Positioning matters. Recovery running matters. If Araujo is setting the standard defensively, Frimpong

item.title: Eight-time champion Marquez to retire from MotoGP
item.description: Marc Marquez's eight MotoGP titles have come between 2013 and 2026 [Getty Images] MotoGP champion Marc Marquez has said he will retire days after clinching a record-equalling eighth title. The 33-year-old Spaniard clinched the 2026 world championship in Portugal last weekend, putting him level with Giacomo Agostini and one clear of modern great Valentino Rossi. The Ducati rider had extended his contract until 2028 in June but will now end his professional career after the final race of the season in Valencia on Sunday. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of the journey," he said. "I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have." Marquez won his first title in 2013 and remains the only rider to win a MotoGP championship in his rookie year. He began his MotoGP career with Honda, winning six titles in seven seasons up to 2019. After joining Gresini Racing - the satellite Ducati team - for 2024, he spent the past two seasons with the Italian outfit's factory team - winning the championship in both. "It is official," read a team statement. "Marc Marquez has decided to retire from MotoGP, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the Ducati Lenovo team." Is Marquez MotoGP's greatest of all time?

item.title: 'That's his problem!' - Vinicius Jr handed blunt reality check by Jose Mourinho as Real Madrid boss demands collective sacrifice ahead of Alaves clash
item.description: FBL-EUR-C1-REAL MADRID-INTER MILAN - AFP Jose Mourinho has sent a clear message to Vinicius Jr and the rest of his Real Madrid stars, insisting that individual reputations mean nothing compared to the needs of the collective. Speaking ahead of the clash with Alaves, the Portuguese coach made it clear that even the biggest names at the Bernabeu must accept their role for the good of the team. Mourinho dismisses guaranteed starting spots The 'Special One' has rejected the idea of a fixed starting line-up at Real Madrid ahead of Saturday night’s La Liga clash against Deportivo Alaves. Addressing the media, the Portuguese coach faced repeated questions over whether Vinicius Jr has done enough to reclaim a regular berth. Mourinho insisted recent speculation around Vinicius’s future and his compatibility with Real's record signing Yan Diomande carries no weight inside the club. While acknowledging the Brazilian has improved, he stressed that team unity always overrides individual standing. 'That's his problem!' Asked how Vinicius compares to Kylian Mbappe and Jude Bellingham - with Bellingham benched only once this season - Mourinho delivered a blunt verdict, attributing their heavy involvement strictly to superior displays. "That’s his problem, not mine," Mourinho said of Vinicius's place in the side. "Mbappe and Bellingham are on the same level as everyone else. If they end up on the bench someday… that’s just how it is. The collective goal is above the individual. The difference lies in their incomparable performance compared to the rest." He also dismissed hints of rivalry between Vinicius and Diomande after their recent celebrations together: "It’s not about competition, we’re all together and we all want the same thing. We’re achieving stability and it seems your objective is to create this doubt. Nobody on the team wants that." Squad depth and unity driving Madrid's resurgence Over his five months in charge, Mourinho has built a steady environment that contrasts with last season’s dressing-room problems. That depth showed when Thibaut Courtois missed his only game through illness, allowing Andriy Lunin to step in and prove decisive. "We have been together for five months and we haven’t had any issues," Mourinho explained. "People want to play; nobody likes being left out or not getting minutes. The collective objective will overcome any individual egos." Title pressure mounts as transfer stance becomes clear Beating Alaves on Saturday will seal an 11th straight win across all competitions for Los Blancos, who have won every match since the first international break and thrashed PSV Eindhoven 5-1 in the Champions League this week. Victory will also pile pressure on La Liga leaders Barcelona, who sit three points ahead before playing on Sunday. With two months left until the transfer window opens, Mourinho also shut down squad exit or arrival talk: "I don’t want anyone coming in and out. I don’t want any transfer rumours."

item.title: Argyle's fit-again Oseni making up for lost time
item.description: Owen Oseni has featured as a substitute in Plymouth's past two League One games [Shutterstock] Plymouth Argyle striker Owen Oseni hopes he can re-establish himself in the side after returning to full fitness. The 23-year-old, who won his first cap for Nigeria over the summer, has recovered from an ankle injury he suffered in late September. At that time, he had only just returned to fitness after injuring his thigh late in pre-season. "It was devastating for me, for my support system, for my family," he told BBC Radio Devon. "It's all part of the game but I don't think I've ever experienced this side of the game, picking up two injuries in such quick succession. "So it was good to learn, just experience that part of the game and just make sure I stay focused, I do my work in the gym and try to come back as quick as I can to help the lads." Plymouth Argyle striker Oseni suffers injury blow Plymouth target attacking signing after Oseni injury Plymouth striker Oseni makes Nigeria debut Oseni has not started a league game since Argyle's 2-2 draw with Exeter City in April. His only starts since then have come in the Jersey Mike's Trophy - he was injured in the 5-1 win over Crystal Palace Under-21s in September before returning in the win over Swindon Town earlier this month. But with Will Evans suspended and fellow forward Bim Pepple also returning to fitness, Oseni has the chance to impress when Argyle travel to Wigan Athletic on Saturday, having featured from the bench in the past two matches. "Owen has been training well this week, been really clean in training, looks fitter and fitter," head coach Tom Cleverley said. "He'll be beneficial for the minutes last week, even though they weren't 30 of his most enjoyable ones - I don't mean for him personally, I thought he did fine, but as a team we weren't at it. "Owen's ready to start and he brings us that penetration that we won't miss without Will playing. "Stylistically they're similar players and [he has] every chance of playing this weekend." Owen Oseni suffered an injury-hit start to the 2026-27 season [Shutterstock] Oseni moved to Argyle from St Mirren in the summer of 2025, having never played in the English Football League before. He scored 10 goals across 33 appearances in all competitions last season as Argyle narrowly missed out on the play-off places. "All I can do is just not focus on the games I miss and just focus on the remaining games," Oseni added. "I can only do myself justice in performing and having the lads achieve what we want to achieve." All the latest Plymouth Argyle news

item.title: Will Stein explains his decision to not call plays for Kentucky Football
item.description: Will Stein’s debut season as a head coach has been a success. The last three games have brought some negativity within the fanbase, but overall, and especially if you can go win the Governor’s Cup to get your eighth win of the season, it’s a successful year one. Stein took over a program with a difficult schedule and not a ton of pieces returning, and entered the year with a betting over/under of 4.5 wins, and got the over on that on October 10 when Kentucky stunned LSU in its second straight victory after beating South Carolina in the same fashion a week earlier. Well, going into the season, there was one decision Stein made that turned some heads and brought some questioning. He said he wouldn’t be calling the offense and that he wants to be a great head coach rather than just an offensive mind. Now, he did mention it’ll have his input, and he won’t abandon it completely, but he would allow the offensive play-calling to be done by former LSU offensive coordinator Joe Sloan. Why is that? Well, Stein answered that with a detailed explanation this week. “I think as a competitor, you want to be in that spot,” Stein said. “But I know for the good of the entire organization, not just the on-the-field play, but recruiting, sports strength and conditioning, our training room, nutrition, fundraising, everything that embodies being a head coach in today’s college football, it was important for me to be at my best for the entirety of the organization. “What we do on Saturdays is really a collection of everybody in our offensive staff room, defensive staff room, special teams room, and using that collaboration and the brain power that we have to formulate the best possible plan that we feel like can go win a football game. And just because I’m not saying it over the mic to the quarterback doesn’t mean that I don’t have my hands in those decisions. “I feel like Joe Sloan has done a fantastic job this season. We’ve battled through ups and downs and adversity. And what I love about Joe is his confidence, his ability to communicate, his ability to connect with players.” Stein then added more on Sloan, saying, “The confidence that he gives our players and our team is really special. And so I’ve been very proud of him and developing this relationship that we have here at Kentucky together.” Stein certainly acknowledged the dip in scoring production in the last three contests after scoring only six against Tennessee, 14 against Florida, and 14 at Missouri, but shows some excitement in the potential of the offense in Saturday’s game against Louisville and onto the postseason. So far, it’s been a success to have Sloan call the plays, with a little bit of Stein’s input during game-planning. Let’s hope this offense can find a way to take care of it, score the ball, and get back to the way it showed earlier in the season.

item.title: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun
item.description: ‘He has come back with a different attitude’ – Filipe Luís pays tribute to Monaco forward Folarin Balogun Filipe Luís has paid tribute to Folarin Balogun’s (25) attitude since returning from the most recent international break. The USMNT forward netted a brace as AS Monaco beat Hearts in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday night. Paris Brunner missed the game in Scotland due to a muscular injury, so it was a chance for Balogun to re-establish himself at Monaco. The former Arsenal man missed the start of the season due to injury and his summer was also marked by the episode of his failed move to Everton. Since returning to fitness, Balogun has failed to replicate the kind of form that saw him become the subject of a €50m approach from Everton. Speaking last week, Filipe Luís evoked the American’s situation: “ For me, it’s very simple. Monaco is bigger than any player. It’s bigger than everybody. And I want players who want to be here, of course. And I need Balogun to feel that he belongs here, that he wants to play here, because then if he plays, he scores goals; it’s going to be easier to make him fulfil his objective .” Just days before, Balogun had reaffirmed his ambition to leave Monaco in the near future. Luís has now praised the forward, who he says has returned from this month’s international break “with a different attitude.” ”He had a summer that was difficult to come to terms with , like Lamine Camara, who was also close to leaving. It is difficult to experience, especially after having played in the World Cup and having heard so many rumours in the press. That also explains why he found it difficult to come back. “Since he came back in November, he has really come back with a different attitude. He is a super player who could still leave in January but until then, he is still a Monaco player and I hope that I will still be able to benefit from him,” said Luís after his brace in the win over Hearts (2-3). GFFN | Luke Entwistle

item.title: AI boom leaves network operators waiting up to 18 months for kit
item.description: The AI building boom is driving up optical networking equipment prices and stretching delivery times to as much as 18 months, according to network operator RETN. RETN says that network operators and telcos are now directly competing with AI datacenters for chips and other components. As Reg readers will be aware, memory prices have soared by four or five times over the past year or so, but RETN says optical networking equipment prices have risen by around 50 percent since the start of 2026. Worse are the extended delivery times, with optical network kit that used to arrive within three months now taking 12 to 15, and some orders taking up to 18 months. This is as bad as, if not worse than, the shortages during the pandemic, when chip supply problems left network vendors unable to fulfill orders . The issue now is that because of the AI boom, demand is outpacing supplies. In its report, "AI, Connected," RETN says developers building outside established datacenter hubs may need to involve network carriers two to five years before opening. The sudden demand for network kit from hyperscalers and AI campuses is only one factor, RETN says. Raw material shortages, skilled labor shortages, energy constraints, geopolitical tensions, and logistical challenges are also compounding the issue. However, it concedes that many carriers didn't help themselves by previously postponing network upgrades to cut expenditure. That work has now become unavoidable at the worst possible time. Network diversity is now seen as a must-have, the report says. Where customers were once satisfied with two routes to long-haul destinations, they expect operators to provide four or more redundant routes now. The aim is to prevent a single failure from taking down critical services. Multiple connections are only useful protection if they avoid shared physical failure points, such as the same ducts or cable routes. A diverse circuit might cost €1,800 ($1,975) a month instead of €600 ($658), it claims, but an outage could prove far more costly. RETN also says AI datacenters are moving away from populated areas to remote locations, where access to suitable land, power and water may be easier to come by. Hyperscalers are building in the Nordics, where land is affordable, the climate is cooler, and plenty of renewable energy is available. Remote sites may lack the fiber infrastructure needed to connect them to other datacenters and customers. The Register reported on this issue earlier this year. For sites close to cities, developers often fund the fiber themselves, which adds just a few percent to the total project cost. But over longer distances, the case becomes harder to make, and carriers are understandably reluctant to build a long-haul route to serve a single remote site. item.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy. In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary. item.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
item.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. The German international nevertheless welcomed the response after halftime, which helped lift Ilzer’s side to 15th place in the Europa League standings. Thursday

item.title: MotoGP Valencia GP: Marco Bezzecchi leads Marc Marquez in cold FP1
item.description: Motorsport photo Marco Bezzecchi set the pace in the opening practice for the Valencia Grand Prix, leading the soon-to-be-retiring Marc Marquez. Just before the track action began on a cold but sunny Circuit Ricardo Tormo, Marquez announced his shock decision to retire from MotoGP at the end of the weekend, sending shockwaves down the paddock. Read Also: Marc Marquez announces immediate retirement from MotoGP in bombshell announcement Alberto Puig on shock Marc Marquez retirement: 'I'm not surprised, it's the right decision' As the crowd remained in disbelief, Raul Fernandez set the early pace aboard the Trackhouse Aprilia, becoming the first rider to break the 1m31s barrier in FP1. About halfway through the session, Marquez moved to the top of the timesheets for Ducati with a 1m30.691s, before Bezzecchi dethroned him by just 0.010s to put Aprilia back at the front. With ambient temperature remaining at just 12C, no further improvements followed in the closing stages of the session, allowing Bezzecchi to hold on to the top spot with his time of 1m30.681s. Fernandez’s early benchmark also remained good enough for third place, with Fermin Aldeguer grabbing fourth for Gresini. Fifth place went to Alex Marquez on the second Gresini Ducati, while Pedro Acosta was the best of the KTM riders in sixth. Johann Zarco crashed with just a minute left on the clock in FP1, but the LCR rider hung on to seventh place and finished the session as the lead Honda. Fabio di Giannantonio was next up in eighth, while the top 10 was completed by the Aprilias of factory rider Jorge Martin and Trackhouse bike of Ai Ogura. Yamaha’s charge was led by Fabio Quartararo in 11th, while Pol Espargaro finished a solid 12th while substituting for Maverick Vinales at Tech3. Apart from Zarco, Jack Miller also crashed late in the session, hitting the deck on his Pramac Yamaha at Turn 2. Competing in his first MotoGP weekend since Malaysia, Joan Mir posted the 18th fastest time aboard the factory Honda, five spots behind team-mate Luca Marini. To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.title: ‘4-1-12-5’: CSK star Jamie Overton demolishes Australia with phenomenal spell at the Gabba
item.description: ‘4-1-12-5’: CSK star Jamie Overton demolishes Australia with phenomenal spell at the Gabba originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: England's Jamie Overton took five wickets for 12 runs as Australia were bowled out cheaply. Australia's 108 at the Gabba is their lowest T20I total on home soil. The Chennai Super Kings seamer had never taken more than three wickets in a T20I. Jamie Overton produces career-best figures as Australia collapses at the Gabba Harry Brook put Australia in at the Brisbane Cricket Ground on Friday with the T20I series level at 1-1, and by the end of the innings the decision had been vindicated in the most emphatic way available. Jamie Overton returned 5 for 12 from his four overs, one of which was a wicket maiden, as Australia were bowled out for 108 in 16.5 overs. The 32-year-old Surrey seamer had taken 31 wickets in 27 T20Is before this match and had never managed more than three in an innings, his previous best being 3 for 18. JAMIE OVERTON: 4-1-12-5 😍 A Phenomenal spell by Overton, he got Double wicket maiden, five wickets for just 12 runs from 4 overs, The CSK Boy in Gabba. — Johns (@CricCrazyJohns) on X Beyond this, Overton was also clocked at 141 kilometres per hour during the spell and had four of his wickets by the end of his fourth over. The fifth followed on the final delivery of it. MORE: CSK auction targets: Who will they buy in IPL 2027 mini-auction? How Australia slipped to their lowest home total in T20 internationals Australia had started well enough. Sam Harper made 26 off 14 balls and Jake Fraser-McGurk 22 off 11 before Overton had the latter caught by Tom Banton at long-on, and the innings never recovered from that point. Nikhil Chaudhary was dropped on 19 and then holed out at long-on off Overton, and Tim David hooked straight to Henry Crocombe at fine leg. Joel Davies top-edged to Sam Curran for three, and Ben Dwarshuis edged behind for a four-ball duck to complete the double-wicket maiden. Liam Dawson gave the innings no relief from the other end, taking 3 for 16 to remove Mitch Marsh for 11, Harper and Adam Zampa. Mitchell Owen was run out for 16 by Phil Salt, and Curran bowled Billy Stanlake before finishing the innings with a maiden. The 108 is the lowest total Australia have made in a T20I at home. England began their chase needing 109 to take a 2-1 lead, with two matches to follow at the Sydney Cricket Ground on Sunday and in Canberra on Wednesday. MORE: CSK star supports team's decision to appoint MS Dhoni as mentor What Jamie Overton's spell means for Chennai Super Kings ahead of IPL 2027 Chennai Super Kings signed Overton at his base price of ₹1.5 crore at the 2025 mega auction and retained him for the 2027 season alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad, Sanju Samson, Shivam Dube and Noor Ahmad. He has not yet become a fixture in their XI. A spell like this one is the argument for changing that. Chennai released Matt Henry and Zak Foulkes

item.title: Syrian referee refutes ‘drunk’ accusations as ‘insult and defamation’
item.description: A referee has hit back at claims he was “drunk” while officiating an AFC Champions League Two match. Footage has been widely shared on social media of Syrian referee Hanna Hattab looking visibly disoriented during a match between Iran 's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates . One particular incident raised eyebrows when Hattab showed a yellow card to Al Jazira’s goalkeeper for a foul that happened close to the halfway line, 40 yards away from him. Hattab was then replaced at half-time with the fourth official taking over for the remainder of the game, which Al Jazira won 1-0. Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following erratic decision-making as similar accusations flooded in online. But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has refuted the allegations as “insult and defamation”, threatening legal action. He wrote in a statement on Facebook: “I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands. Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them. “I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.” He also said he would issue a further statement following contact with the Syrian Arab Football Federation (SFA) which will “clarify all the details and facts related to what happened ... with full transparency and clarity.” Omani journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian football, has since claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus". The SFA have also put out a statement standing in support of Hattab, while stating it has requested his medical report from the match. “The Main Referees Committee of the Syrian Arab Football Federation confirms that it stands in full support of international referee Mr Hana Khattab regarding the incident he was subjected to, following reassurance about his health,” it said. “This comes after the committee was reassured of his well-being, following a number of discussions on social media concerning the incident. The committee emphasises its full support for him and its commitment to following up on the matter in all its details and developments. “In this regard, the committee has requested that the Syrian Football Referees Committee provide the medical report relating to the referee, the match observers' report and the referee assessor's report. This is in order to establish the circumstances of the incident accurately and comprehensively and to complete the necessary procedures in this matter. “The committee also confirms that it will provide the relevant authorities and the public with the findings as soon as the requested reports are

item.title: Shaquille O’Neal thinks Anthony Edwards can ruin Timberwolves if he fails to notice one thing
item.description: Credit: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto/David Berding via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have been doing quite well even without Anthony Edwards, and Shaquille O’Neal has sent the superstar a warning about his eventual return. Anthony Edwards has been out indefinitely since he had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee late in October. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has missed the entirety of November, and will likely miss all of December and a fair amount of time in January as well. The Timberwolves haven’t struggled all that much in his absence, either. LaMelo Ball has fit the team like a glove, and they have a 14-5 record going into Friday’s game against the Memphis Grizzlies. With that in mind, Shaquille O’Neal recently shared some advice for the young superstar for when he does return. Shaquille O’Neal says Anthony Edwards will have to ensure he doesn’t disrupt team rhythm after returning The Timberwolves have played excellent team ball in Edwards’ absence. He was averaging over 33 points per game in his four games this season. Since he’s been out, though, the team has five players averaging between 12 points to 19 points per game. No one star has been dominating, and this style has been working quite well. So Shaq thinks Edwards will have to be careful with that when he does come back. “I think it’s going to be up to Anthony Edwards,” O’Neal said. “Because right now, he has to see how the guys are playing. Because they’re only playing like this because they’re eating. See, a lot of time when he has the ball, they’re just sitting in the corner, and they’re really out of rhythm. “Now that he’s not there, LaMelo’s kicking it to a damn rhythm. So he has to see this. So when he gets back, he’s going to have to get his and keep his guys in rhythm.” The likes of Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu, and Jonathan Kuminga are beginning to truly establish themselves within the context of the team. If Edwards can come back and figure out a seamless fit, no team will want to face off against the Timberwolves in the playoffs this season. item.title: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling
item.description: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling Joshua Kimmich made headlines earlier this week after publicly criticising the Bayern Munich hierarchy over their comments on Jamal Musiala's neurological condition and the possibility of adjusting his salary. His comments subsequently sparked speculation over whether he could face disciplinary action, potentially in the form of a fine. However, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund has now made it clear that no such punishment is being considered. “We never discussed that, and imposing a fine was never a topic of conversation. We're really looking forward and focusing on the upcoming games,” Freund said at Friday's press conference. Sitting alongside Freund, head coach Vincent Kompany was also asked about the vice-captain's outspoken comments but declined to elaborate. Instead, he emphasised that internal matters should remain behind closed doors. “I understand what this question is getting at. However, I can't help you any further with these matters at the moment. We have our bubble, and that's how it will stay," Kompany said. “That doesn't mean we simply applaud everything internally. We tell each other the truth and openly address what hasn't gone well. But I protect these matters, and I lead by example in that regard. “If I were to comment on other issues now, I wouldn't be living up to that standard. My priority is the game against Hamburg.”

item.title: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic
item.description: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic Barcelona are facing growing concern over an injury crisis affecting several sections of the club, with the men’s and women’s first teams, Barça Atlètic and even the basketball side all struggling with player absences, according to a report from SPORT . The mounting problems have intensified fears that an increasingly congested calendar is taking a physical toll on the club’s athletes across all the divisions. Despite investment in medical staff, rehabilitation support and injury prevention, Barcelona have yet to find a solution to the growing number of setbacks. The situation is particularly troubling for the football department, where Hansi Flick’s first team has repeatedly been forced to manage injuries during demanding stretches of the season. Unfortunately, however, the concern is not limited to the senior squad, with the reserve team also experiencing a difficult run. A packed calendar is testing Barcelona’s prevention work Hansi Flick strengthened the first-team physical preparation staff in July by bringing in Benjamin Kugel , aiming to improve conditioning and reduce late-season injury problems. Hansi Flick has been dealing with player shortages, especially in defence, this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yet muscle injuries remain a recurring issue amid international travel and matches every three or four days. Specifically, the stretch involving Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid illustrated the cost. Eric García, Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart and Dani Olmo suffered injuries during that period, while Gerard Martin also experienced discomfort . The sequence left Flick managing absences during a demanding run of fixtures. Barça Atlètic faces the most severe shortage The reserve team has been hit especially hard. Before facing Girona B, Juliano Belletti was dealing with a shortage caused by injuries and international call-ups, with reports counting more than 20 unavailable players. Barcelona requested that the fixture be postponed, but it went ahead. Barcelona have suffered several injuries this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The match brought further damage, as Dani Avila and Ibrahim Diarra were injured , while other players finished with physical problems. Barça Atlètic subsequently lost Mirza Catovic in the derby against Espanyol B. Barcelona confirmed that Catovic had suffered a fibula fracture and would be out for around four months, taking the reserve side’s injury list to 12. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s women’s side is also dealing with a difficult injury situation, while the basketball team has been managing absences during a packed domestic and EuroLeague schedule. The pattern across several departments makes the issue bigger than an isolated run of bad luck. Barcelona have invested in prevention and recovery, but workload, travel and limited rest continue to challenge those measures.

item.title: Ex-Patriots quarterback Joe Milton steals the show on Thanksgiving
item.description: With one former New England Patriots quarterback in the broadcast booth, another played the game of his life. Joe Milton, under the watchful eye of Tom Brady, led the Philadelphia Eagles to a 39-38 road victory over the Dallas Cowboys on Thanksgiving. And even on a day that saw the likes of Patrick Mahomes, Josh Allen, Caleb Williams, Jared Goff and Dak Prescott all line up under center, it was the third-year QB that stole the show. Milton completed 21 of 31 pass attempts for 331 yards with three touchdowns and an interception. He also led the game-winning drive when he marched Philadelphia’s offense into kicker Jake Elliott’s field goal range in the late fourth quarter, helping the Eagles overcome what was a 21-point deficit in the late third quarter. In addition, he proved why his “Bazooka Joe” nickname was well earned: he threw some truly spectacular passes. Every time Joe Milton made the craziest throw of the year vs the Cowboys 5 different times. pic.twitter.com/lVuL46DCmH — Cam (@42Cyc) November 27, 2026 Milton completed six of his 11 deep pass attempts versus the Cowboys, gaining 188 yards and scoring three touchdowns. He finished the game with 0.308 expected points added per play, a completion percentage 12.1 points over expectation, and an average of 17.3 air yards — ranking first among all six of the quarterbacks taking the field on Thursday. Whether he can build on the successful outing in front of a national audience will be seen. For Milton, however, it was a high point on what had been a rollercoaster of a career so far. That rollercoaster, of course, that started when the Patriots selected him in the sixth round of the 2024 draft. Milton was brought in in the same draft class as third overall pick Drake Maye, whose status as the Patriots’ future face of the franchise was never questioned. This, in turn, put his fellow then-rookie on a path to backup duty; but with veteran Jacoby Brissett also under contract at the time, not even that materialized. He ended up playing just one game as a rookie, the season finale against Buffalo a mere hours before head coach Jerod Mayo was fired. Milton completed 22 of 29 passes in that contest for 241 yards and a touchdown, leading New England to its fourth game of the year (and to drop out of the first overall draft pick). With a new regime under Mike Vrabel coming in, however, his days were numbered. In April of 2025, Milton and a seventh-round pick were sent to Dallas for a fifth-rounder. Through a series of follow-up trade, Patriots turned that selection into kicker Andy Borregales, long snapper Julian Ashby and cornerback Kobee Minor. Milton, meanwhile, played four games in his first season as a Cowboy but lost the QB2 competition this summer. He started his 2026 campaign on the Dallas practice squad, but was signed off of it by the Eagles in October. A month later, and with him now serving as Philadelphia’s starter in place of the injured Jalen Hurts, he now got the best of his former team.

item.title: Conflicts, El Nino Worsening Hunger — UN
item.description: UN food agencies warned Friday of worsening hunger over the next six months in 16 mostly African areas, with ongoing conflicts exacerbating already dire conditions in countries like Sudan and Yemen. While armed conflict and violence are the main reasons for acute food insecurity around the globe, dramatic climate events, including El Nino, are another driver, the joint report from the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and the World Food Programme (WFP) said. The Rome-based agencies listed Sudan, South Sudan, Somalia, northern Nigeria and Yemen as the areas of highest concern in its early warning about 16 “hunger hotspots” from December until May 2027. Famine remains a “plausible” risk in parts of Sudan — including North Darfur — and South Sudan, the report found. ‘Alarming levels of displacement’ The indoor cooking setup of a local food vendor, featuring large metal pots resting on industrial gas stoves. The stoves are connected directly to an orange gas cylinder running on the clean, smoke-free biogas produced by the biodigester. (Photo: Nosakhale Akhimien/Channels TV) The risk of worsening hunger comes amid a rise in “political violence events” around the world, up by more than 15 percent over the same period a year earlier, which has prompted “alarming levels of displacement in recent months”, particularly in South Sudan and Yemen. In the five countries most at risk, all repeatedly cited on the hotspot list since 2022, humanitarian assistance has declined by nearly two-thirds over the 2022-2025 period, from $5.1 billion to $2 billion. “While conflict, economic shocks, climate extremes and access constraints have remained the primary drivers of these crises, declining humanitarian resources have reduced the capacity to sustain gains and mitigate worsening conditions,” wrote FAO and WFP. While past humanitarian assistance helped avert famine, “the gains proved fragile and of limited duration: severe acute food insecurity risks — including risk of famine — re-emerged within a few years.” Also classified as a “very high concern” are Afghanistan, the Democratic Republic of Congo — which is also struggling to contend with an outbreak of Ebola — Palestine, and Haiti, where expanding gang violence has displaced 1.5 million people and disrupted humanitarian access. New additions to the list are Chad, Uganda, the Southern Africa region and the Central American Dry Corridor, a tropical dry forest extending from Guatemala to Costa Rica, with the latter two regions expected to be hit by the effects of El Nino, adversely affecting crops. The list also includes Mali, Myanmar and Madagascar. “Targeted humanitarian action is urgently needed to save lives and livelihoods across all hunger hotspots,” read the report. “In hotspots of highest concern, such action is critical to prevent starvation and loss of life.” Too much or little rain El Nino — the ocean warming phenomenon that is disrupting weather patterns globally, provoking devastating droughts or in

item.title: Fabio Cannavaro reveals Liverpool star Virgil van Dijk's desire to play in Serie A amid AC Milan links
item.description: 버질 판데이크 (Virgil van Dijk) - Getty Images Fabio Cannavaro has revealed that Liverpool centre-back Virgil van Dijk expressed a desire to play in Serie A during a conversation at the World Cup. With the Dutchman's contract expiring in June 2027, the Italy legend believes a switch to AC Milan would be an exciting move. Van Dijk eyes Italian football adventure Liverpool could face a battle to keep hold of Van Dijk as speculation grows over his long-term future . The Dutch centre-back has reportedly emerged on Milan's radar ahead of next season. Former Italy international Cannavaro has now added fuel to those rumours in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport . The 2006 Ballon d'Or winner disclosed that Van Dijk is genuinely intrigued by the prospect of testing himself in Italian football. Van Dijk existing deal with Liverpool is set to expire in June 2027, leaving the door open for potential suitors to monitor his availability. Cannavaro backs Dutchman for Milan switch Cannavaro explained that his insight came directly from a personal conversation with the Liverpool defender during the World Cup. Having represented Napoli, Parma, Juventus, and Inter during his own career, the Italian icon believes Milan would be a fitting destination. "I saw him at the World Cup and he told me that he would like to have an experience in Italy," Cannavaro said. "He is very fascinated by it. It would be nice to see Van Dijk at Milan." Physical dominance and the Maldini comparison While Cannavaro is clearly an admirer of Van Dijk's attributes, he also offered a candid tactical assessment of how elite defenders evolve over time. Drawing on his own experiences and an anecdote involving Paolo Maldini, Cannavaro highlighted the vital role of pace in defending. "In recent years, he has combined great physical strength with outstanding speed," Cannavaro noted. "Once, a coach said to Paolo Maldini: 'You turn badly.' And he replied: 'Mister, as long as I get to the ball.'" Cannavaro warned that relying on recovery speed comes with an inevitable caveat later in a player's career. "It was the same for me," he added. "When you are very fast, you can afford a technical error. The problem comes when that speed is no longer there." What next for Van Dijk's future? With Van Dijk's Liverpool contract running until June 2027, the club still hold a strong position regarding his immediate future. However, Milan's reported interest for next season means the Italian side could soon test Liverpool's resolve. Whether Van Dijk decides to act on his fascination with Serie A remains to be seen.

item.title: Botman banned from driving for using phone at wheel
item.description: Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving [PA] Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel. The Newcastle United centre-back pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while using a motor vehicle on a road at Newcastle Magistrates' Court on Wednesday. The 26-year-old was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued. He was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge, the MoJ said. Botman was driving a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone. The Dutchman changed his plea from not guilty to guilty at his court appearance on Wednesday, the MoJ confirmed. Newcastle United signed Botman from Lille in 2022. He has made nine appearances so far this season, scoring one goal. Follow BBC Newcastle on X , Facebook , Nextdoor and Instagram and listen to Radio Newcastle on BBC Sounds .

item.title: ‘We're Still Free to Race': Lewis Hamilton Reveals Ferrari Stance After Las Vegas Chat With Charles Leclerc
item.description: Lewis Hamilton says he and Charles Leclerc are still free to race against each other. (Source: MEGA) Lewis Hamilton has revealed that Ferrari will continue to allow him and his teammate Charles Leclerc to race freely despite their collision at the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend. Hamilton also confirmed that the two drivers have already discussed the incident and are looking to put the tension behind them ahead of the final two rounds of the 2026 season. Speaking to Sky Sports F1 ahead of the Qatar Grand Prix this weekend, Hamilton addressed the situation and confirmed that Ferrari has not changed its approach to allowing its drivers to compete against each other. "We’re still free to race, and I think that’s the ultimate goal of being here," the Briton said. "We want to race, right? Um, but of course we don’t want what happened last week to ever happen. Charles and I had a good sit-down earlier on and had our chat. I think moving forward, I think we can be fine. Lewis Hamilton confirms he and Charles Leclerc remain free to race each other following their collision in Las Vegas. "We're still free to race, and I think that's the ultimate goal of being here. We want to race, right? But of course, we don't want what happened last week to… — Everything Formula (@evrythngformu1a) November 26, 2026 "We do enjoy racing together, and we have a great-we do have a really good relationship. It’s obviously intense. Yeah, in the background, on the outside, it seems a lot more intense than it really is inside". How the Tension Between Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc Escalated in Vegas Hamilton and Leclerc made contact while fighting for sixth place in Las Vegas last weekend, with the Monegasque driver spinning his teammate around and sending him down the order. Leclerc was subsequently handed a 10-second time penalty for causing the collision, while Hamilton managed to recover and finish seventh. Leclerc was classified in 10th after the race. The incident was another flashpoint in an increasingly tense season between Ferrari's two drivers, following previous on-track clashes in Monza and Mexico City. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were first involved in a clash in Monza this season. (Source: MEGA) Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur was particularly critical of Leclerc after the Las Vegas clash, describing the incident as "unacceptable." "It’s a lack of respect for the team, for the sponsors, the same speech as after Mexico. I think we had a clear discussion in Sao Paulo. Today it wasn’t professional," Vasseur said. Hamilton wasn’t the only one to talk about the incident from last week in Qatar. Charles Leclerc Also Addresses Tension With Hamilton Leclerc also opened up about his relationship with Hamilton during the FIA pre-race press conference on Thursday in Qatar, acknowledging that their recent clashes have become a concern for the team.
